checks.name: two independent rules must agree before a byte is deleted, and a <pre> line break is content
the house Matrixify preflight on the FINISHED file, with the live body supplied for a round trip
THE ONE THAT WOULD CORRUPT A LESSON: a newline inside a <pre> is content, not a defect
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] 2.7 and the <pre> code sample still has its line break
checks._why: The two candidates this rule protects are `parameters` and `public static double average(...)`, which are two lines of a Java code sample in the lesson. Joining them produces `parameterspublic static double average` inside a <pre>, which renders, passes every structural check, and teaches a student that a declaration comment and a method signature sit on one line. A deletion is not automatically safe just because it deletes.

checks.name: the second rule is load bearing too: a token nobody has seen must not be joined

checks._why: Rule B is what makes rule A checkable. It knows nothing about <pre> and still rejects the same two, because `parameterspublic` and `argumentsdouble` appear nowhere in the course. Two rules that agree by accident would be one rule; this proves they are reached independently.

checks.name: the only-newlines-moved proof, against the one corruption a byte count cannot see
checks.expect_failure: the repaired body differs from the live body somewhere other than a newline
checks._why: Two earlier cuts of this were refused and both refusals were right. The first guard re-ran the same deletion loop into a second variable and compared them: a tautology. The second was real but nothing could make it fire, because a correct loop never violates it. This mutation deletes the RIGHT NUMBER of bytes at the WRONG OFFSET, one character earlier, so the byte-count guard still passes and only the strip-newlines comparison notices. That is the case this guard exists for and the only one that distinguishes it from the byte count. The expected string is the generator's own refusal message, which appears nowhere on a PASS line.

checks.name: the ld+json rule must prove itself: invalid before, valid after, or it is guessing
checks.find: if (!fixes) { out.push({ unfixable: true, at: start }); continue; }
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] 4.4 an ld+json block that newline-removal cannot fix REFUSES the sheet
checks._why: A block that does not parse, and that removing newlines does not fix, has some other cause: a trailing comma, a bad escape. Silently skipping it ships a body whose structured data is still broken while the sheet reports success. The gate refused the first version of this mutation because nothing on the real page exercises the branch, so the suite now feeds repair() a block broken by a trailing comma and requires the refusal.

checks.name: the browser, which is the only thing that can say whether a student can use the page
checks._why: The suite reasons about bytes. This loads the live body and the repaired body in Chromium and drives the actual widgets: click an option, click Check answer, count graded options, count CodeMirror instances. It reaches the same verdict by a completely different route, and it is the only check that can tell the difference between a page that parses and a page that works.
